Report Description/// THIS IS A CORRECTION TO NRC REPORT # 1464075 /// CORRECT 'COUNTY' IS IN THE 'BETHEL (CENSUS AREA)' NOT 'ANCHORAGE'. CALLER STATES THAT DUE TO THE 'TYPOON HALONG' THAT OCCURRED ON 12OCT2025, THE FOLLOWING 03 VILLAGES NEAR ANCHORAGE WERE ADVERSELY IMPACTED IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: NIGHTNUTE VILLAGE -LAGOON BROKE AND INUNDATED COMMUNITY WITH BAGS OF HUMAN WASTE. KIPNUK -LAGOON BROKE AND INUNDATED COMMUNITY WITH BAGS OF HUMAN WASTE AND VAST AMOUNTS OF DEBRIS. -MIGRATORY BIRDS ARE CURRENTLY NESTING IN THE CONTAMINATED AREA; UTILIZED AS A RESOURCE IN THE VILLAGE, THE COMMUNITY (AND OTHER WILDLIFE) ARE CONSUMING THE NOW CONTAMINATED EGGS. KWIGILLINGOK - A LARGE SECTION OF THE COMMUNITY HAS SUBSIDED FROM THE EVENT BUT ARE INUNDATED WITH 5 FEET WATER AT EVERY HIGH TIDE. - A PIPE AND HEADER AT THE KWIG FUEL FARM (LOCAL BULK TANK FACILITY) IS NOT SECURED AND ACTIVELY DISCHARGES UNKNOWN AMOUNTS OF DIESEL FUEL/KEROSENE HEATING OIL, THEN SETTLES ON THE LAND AT EVERY LOW TIDE; THIS OCCURS EVERY TIDE CYCLE. -A LARGE SECTION OF HOMES/ THE BOARDWALK HAS ALSO SETTLED ON TOP OF THE AFFECTED PIPELINE. EXACT NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS EVACUATED IS ESTIMATED TO BE AROUND 3,000. CALLER STATES THAT THE DELAY IN REPORTING IS DUE TO THE FACT THAT EVERYTHING FROZE DIRECTLY AFTER THE DISASTER AND ARE CURRENTLY AT A POINT WHERE THE IMPACT HAS BEEN DISCOVERED. /// THIS IS A CORRECTION TO NRC REPORT # 1464075 ///

Report Description
PORT STAFF WAS NOTIFIED BY A TUG OWNER THAT THERE WAS A SHEEN IN THE SOUTHEAST CORNER OF THE HARBOR NEAR HIS NON-OPERATING TUGBOAT, BUT ADAMANT THAT THE SHEEN WAS OUTSIDE THE HARD BOOM AND THEREFORE NOT FROM HIS VESSEL. FACILITY WAS EXPERIENCING HIGH SOUTHERNLY WINDS AND SEAS AT THE TIME BUT SHEEN WAS TRAPPED AGAINST THE SOUTH WALL AND NOT AFFECTED BY THE WIND. PORT STAFF DEPLOYED SORBENT BOOM WITH A SKIFF TO CAPTURE MOST OF THE SHEEN AND TRAP IT AGAINST THE WALL UNTIL STORM CONDITIONS DIMINISH AND IT CAN BE RETRIEVED. STAFF SUSPECTS THE SHEEN DID ESCAPE FROM AROUND THE END OF THE TUG'S BOOM BUT IT CAN'T BE PROVEN SINCE THERE'S A STORM DRAIN IN THE SAME AREA THAT DUMPS STREET RUNOFF INTO THE HARBOR DURING RAINY PERIODS.

FACILITY WAS EXPERIENCING HIGH SOUTHERNLY WINDS AND SEAS AT THE TIME BUT SHEEN WAS TRAPPED AGAINST THE SOUTH WALL AND NOT AFFECTED BY THE WIND. PORT STAFF DEPLOYED SORBENT BOOM WITH A SKIFF TO CAPTURE MOST OF THE SHEEN AND TRAP IT AGAINST THE WALL UNTIL STORM CONDITIONS DIMINISH AND IT CAN BE RETRIEVED. STAFF SUSPECTS THE SHEEN DID ESCAPE FROM AROUND THE END OF THE TUG'S BOOM BUT IT CAN'T BE PROVEN SINCE THERE'S A STORM DRAIN IN THE SAME AREA THAT DUMPS STREET RUNOFF INTO THE HARBOR DURING RAINY PERIODS.
